_: spine:leros-phase-three as it stood on 15 November 2026 at midday, before Matthew's reconfiguration that afternoon; kept word for word.

1.2: WHAT IT COSTS — the work: weft's building and David's time, which phase three names (4.6). It uses what the beach already has: its standard for places, the earth beach, and the app as it stands. Laid out this way, every possibility stays open, including one day an RPG with other players, without anyone building one now. (Until 14 November this line said 'nothing beyond the work'.)
1.3: WHAT IT CHANGES ON COMMUNITY RECOVERY'S BEACH — the landscape is kept as a map the app draws (4.7), so no world blocks are added yet. The meeting room stays off; it was never used. Each place's room for talk opens only as 4.4 says.
1.8: DECIDE — is this the order of work, with these owners? Asked of David, weft and Matthew. ANSWERED 14 November by Matthew: yes, with weft's three changes (leros-phase-three:weft), and weft as the one builder (1.19).
1._: THE BUILD — weft is the one builder of the app for phase three (1.19). Weft builds See it as first, then the journey, on a private copy with made-up people in every ring; David and Matthew both walk it as every ring; then it goes live one screen at a time, with before and after screenshots, as the app's house rules say. The run-through of every screen (1.15) runs alongside, starting with the meeting notes. The gift map follows. Matthew keeps and steers; weft builds in the app and on the beach; David answers for the standard and the earth. Each piece is carried as a thread once its decision stands.
1.4: FOR BUILDERS, WHAT WE BUILD NOW — in this order, each piece useful alone and done when its line says. Weft builds; Matthew steers and decides; David answers for the standard and the earth (1.199). Every piece goes first on the private copy with made-up people in every ring, is walked by David and Matthew as every ring, then goes live one screen at a time. (1) SEE IT AS (1.198): done when Matthew and David can view the app as someone outside, someone who has asked to join, a member from day one, a member, a welcomer, a leader and a supporter; nothing is written as anyone; nobody's days or notes open; builders stay out of members' lists; and the leaders have been told. (2) THE STEPS (1.193): done when one steps block holds the steps a person can take, in plain words, at the standards' addresses, each saying who it is for; each person's path is their own mirror of it; the Leadership Team can change a step without code; and Today's chosen step reads from it. (3) TODAY AND THE HEART (1.191, 1.192, 4.9): done when the step chosen for me follows its order; Keep today offers where today rests and never requires it; tap, hold and slide, and hold and let go all work, with every place also in Everything and reachable by keyboard and screen reader; and the heart's shadow follows the sun over Wellingborough. The Leadership Team shapes the thumb menu first. (4) WHAT I BRING, FIRST (1.194, 4.2): done when each part (hope, something I know about, something I can do or make, something I care about, groups I'm part of, what helps me take part) has its own choice of who sees it; it is offered first on Today and never required; and nothing about health, treatment or the law is asked. (5) MY GARDEN AND OUR WOOD (1.195, 1.196): done when my garden shows its owner alone the hope seed, gifts, days, flowers for steps taken and six circles of where my days rest, with no numbers; and our wood replaces the standards garden, fed by steps as community evidence with no names. (6) THE GIFT MAP (1.197, 1.11): done when peer leaders see hopes and gifts by place and time, each part there only on its owner's yes, with the cards of things that need doing beside it, and our helper's notices reach the peer leaders only. (7) THE LIGHTHOUSE'S PICTURES (1.17): done when paths and liveliness show by place and by week, a place lights only once a few people have been there, and nothing names anyone. ALONGSIDE: the run-through of every screen (1.15), the meeting notes first.
1.5: FOR BUILDERS, WHERE THE DATA LIVES — every block the app reads and writes stands on Community Recovery's own beach, beach.communityrecovery.life (the app's config.js); the standards family alone stands on beach.happyseaurchin.com. WHAT STANDS: passport:<name>, a person's card, its 1 what I can offer and its 2 my hope, its 3 'What I could use' until 13 November, whose words stay and are never reused for anything else; now:<name>, a person's kept days, sealed with their own words, where today's resting place is kept inside the day; pool:<name>, each person's room; pool:community-recovery, the noticeboard; pool:journey, our story; pool:policies and pool:presentation; the notebooks agreement:<name>, leadership:<name>, learning:<name> and standards:<name>; going, arrivals, where-and-when and the lighthouse; app-words, every word the app shows, kept by the Leadership Team; colour:leadership and colour:welcomers, the private rooms. WHAT IS NEW, each named by weft and written here before it is built: the steps block and each person's path; each part of What I bring with its own choice of who sees it; the record of places visited, kept by place and by week with nothing about any person; and See it as, which writes nothing. For every one the app's house rule holds: before reading or writing at an address, search app.js for every reader of that address; one address, one meaning.
1.6: FOR BUILDERS, THE RULES THAT DON'T BEND — nothing about a person is counted or scored; the app speaks in I and we, in plain words with no beach terms, run through the language engine and chosen by the Leadership Team; every gesture has a tap and a plain list beside it, and the app meets WCAG 2.2 AA; every change carries before and after screenshots at 380 pixels, dark, with the live beach's data, listing anything that disappeared, which must be nothing unless asked; a change never leaves a screen plainer or less alive; one builder per screen; a member's kept days are read by nobody but the member; and every share is a yes, one thing at a time (the app's house rules in its CLAUDE.md; 1.13; 4.3).
1.7: FOR BUILDERS, WHAT IS NOT IN THIS BUILD, AND WHERE TO ASK — not now: a world on the beach for the landscape (4.7); each place's room for talk, until 4.4's two conditions hold; private talk between two members; any AI inside the app beyond our helper (5.2); Sundial on the phone and recipes (5.4, 5.5); offering the app to other LEROs (1.111). Ask in the proposal's room, pool:leros-phase-three, or on a piece's thread once it has one; answer a decision in your own reading, leros-phase-three:<your name>. Matthew decides what the app is for its people, David answers for the beach's standard and the earth, and weft for how it is built; where they differ, Matthew decides, and the reason is written where the decision stands.

(3) Today and the heart: not started; the app as it stands has its menu back and no bar at the foot, the bar having been tried and taken out on 14 November (community-recovery #39). 1.2: THE OUTWARD MAP — Community Recovery's app already shows where it sits among the LEROs, from the United Kingdom down to Wellingborough, lit gold with 'We are here', read from the earth beach (earth.beach.happyseaurchin.com). Today that map stops at the town, and the neighbourhood inside it is a list.
1.3: THE GRAFT — by the beach's standard, a place joins a larger world by its address: a region fits where it stands one step from a named neighbour, and everything beneath inherits everything above (pscale:world-genome 2.4). A LERO's landscape joins the earth the same way, its keeper carrying the placing (pscale:world-genome 5).
1.8: DECIDE — should each LERO's place join the earth at its own town, its keeper carrying the placing? Asked of David. Matthew's answer, 14 November: NOT YET, for the reason at 1.111.
1._: EVERY LERO — the same landscape for every LERO, each on a beach of its own: the common, the four neighbourhoods at the standards' four sections, the gate and the gardens, with that LERO's own places inside. Each LERO's place is set where it really is on the earth, so the app's outward map, 'We are here', walks straight into the neighbourhood, and CLERO can read one picture across many LEROs because the same places stand at the same addresses (leros-on-the-commons 1.16). Nothing is copied upward. Decided 14 November: the app is built now ready to be white-labelled, each LERO's name, logo, colours, venues and words kept in settings and blocks and out of the code; it is offered to other LEROs only once phase one's kit, agreement and ground are in place (leros-on-the-commons 1.1113 and 1.1115). Why: the offer isn't ready to go outward (Matthew, 9 November), and building it this way costs nothing extra.

1.2: WHAT STANDS — What I bring already asks asset-based community development's head, hands and heart, and connections: something I know about, something I can do or make, something I care about, groups I'm part of. Hope was asked at Ask to join and dropped from What I bring on 13 November; it comes back (4.2). Introductions show gifts only. Learning together already gathers what members would like to learn.
1.3: THE GROUPS IN IT — who holds each place, members, volunteers, the Leadership Team, welcomers, supporters and visitors, is the register that answers what David named as a gap on the beach: groups, and how people stand in relation to one another and to the place (pscale:world-genome 2.3; the draft at community-recovery-design:Phenomemental 1.296). Supporters are people from partner organisations who help without a vote (4.1).
1.8: DECIDE — what should the map show first, inside the members' circle: gifts at places and times, what members would like to learn, or both? Asked of Matthew and David. GIFTS, LEARNING, BOTH or NOT YET. ANSWERED 14 November by Matthew: BOTH, with hope beside the gifts; needs stay on paper.
1._: THE GIFT MAP — asset-based community development made practical (leros-on-the-commons 1.17), as the first thing the landscape shows: what members say they bring (hope, something they know about, something they can do or make, something they care about, groups they're part of), at which places and when, with what members would like to learn beside it, so peer leaders see who could meet whom and which gifts sit unused. Its loop is Matthew's golden flow, starting from hope: hope, gift, met, changed. Members only, and each part reaches the map only on its owner's yes, item by item. Needs stay on paper, in the welcome conversation. Beside the map stand the community's cards of things that need doing, put up by the Leadership Team, where gifts meet the work (the original proposal's 'wanting to help', brought back). Renamed on 14 November from 'the gift-and-need map': asset-based community development starts from people's gifts and dreams, and starting from need is the deficit lens it was made to replace.

1.2: NOW — moving through the app. Tried on 14 November and taken out the same afternoon at Matthew's word: a bar at the foot of every screen (Me, Us, Today, How we run, More). It sat inside the page, above the help box, and scrolled away with it, so people didn't see it. What stands, decided 14 November: the thumb menu (community-recovery-design:Phenomemental 1.233), hold Today and slide to Us, Me, How we run or More, or just tap, with Everything, the plain list, always beside it; and Today holding my day, the step chosen for me and two side paths (1.19). The Leadership Team shapes the thumb menu before it is built. Any future bar is fixed to the bottom of the screen, stands out from the cards, and comes only if the leaders want one.
1.3: WHAT IT MUST HOLD — every gesture has a tap and a plain list beside it; words stay few, big and plain; nothing is counted and nothing is scored about a person; what is recorded and what is shown are said plainly in the privacy notice (1.17); the app speaks in I and we; and it meets WCAG 2.2 AA, as Community Recovery's accessibility policy promises.
1.4: THE PEOPLE IN IT TODAY — Community Recovery's Leadership Team, founders who appointed one another on 16 October 2026, came into the app on 13 November as its first people and co-producers; by that night seven of the ten founding seats were taken. How they are involved, decided 14 November: a basic standard is designed first by Matthew, David and weft, because there has to be something real to respond to; the leaders are then asked in the app, they name the places and walk the landscape on paper, and anything decided before they were asked stays open to change. Why: co-production is CLERO's second principle and the main principle here (leros-on-the-commons 1.152), and the app can already carry each leader's yes, suggested change or not sure in their own notebook. (Until 14 November this line said nothing in the proposal asked anything of them.)
1.8: DECIDE — is the view from the lighthouse right: each person sees where they are, what's waiting for them and where life is happening, and sees others only where they have acted in the open? Asked of David and Matthew. ANSWERED 14 November by Matthew: yes, with paths shown by place and by week (1.17).
1._: HOW IT WORKS FOR THE PEOPLE IN IT — standing at the lighthouse, a person sees where they are, what is waiting for them, and where the life of the community is: who's going to Tuesday's social, a new note on the noticeboard, a word left for them. Others are seen only where they have acted in the open, on the noticeboard, in who's going, in Our story, in a word left on someone's page; a garden lights only for its owner. The app gets clearer now, and moving through the place itself comes as the app matures.
1.5: THE RUN-THROUGH — every screen walked in the order a person meets it, as a member, a leader, a welcomer and a visitor would: what it is for, what I can do there, where I go next, how it looks and reads, and what must stay. Each screen's keep list and changes are written beneath its design, and built a batch at a time to the app's house rule: before and after at phone width, nothing removed unless asked, never plainer or less alive than it was. The meeting notes come first, made readable and agreed in the app, because the Leadership Team is in it now. One builder per screen at a time (1.19).
1.6: WHAT IT IS FOR EACH PERSON — the product this phase serves, described person by person with what each can do now, what comes next and what comes later: someone curious, a member, volunteers, the Leadership Team, supporters, learning and development, the organisation and the network (community-recovery-design:Phenomemental 8.5). A LERO app, Community Recovery's first, to be white-labelled for any LERO once it is firm: the place, the screens and the standards belong to every LERO; the names, the real places, the brand and the words are each LERO's own.
1.7: WHAT THE LIGHTHOUSE SHOWS — the life of the place, drawn so people can feel it: the rhythm of the week, with the sessions and the life between them; the paths most walked and the places most lively; hopes meeting gifts, the golden flow; our wood growing as the evidence comes in; and the people we meet. Paths and liveliness are shown by place and by week, never who and never by the hour, and a place lights only once a few people have been there. Each picture comes from what actually happens and is seen by members only. A record is kept of which places in the app are visited, shown only as how lively each place is, and the privacy notice says so. Decided 14 November at Matthew's word: paths are shown because they show there is life. Claude's weighed concern, kept here: with only a few people a path can point to one person, which is why it is shown only by place and by week. Leaders and supporters see only the pattern across everyone; steps done in the open stay visible as now; one person's path stays in their own garden.

9.1: TODAY — keep today; one step chosen for me, shown big; two small side paths. The pick is first what someone is waiting on me for (for a leader, the meeting notes or the constitution), then What I bring until I've answered or chosen Later, then the next step on my path. Why: Today holds my day and what is waiting for me; links gathering on it showed a design problem.
9.2: MOVING — the thumb menu (1.12), with Everything, the plain list, beside every gesture, as WCAG 2.2 AA and Matthew's notes require.
9.3: THE STEPS — weft's journey, built the pscale way: one block holds the steps a person can take, in plain words (read our safeguarding policy; say yes to part one of the constitution; come to the next meeting), at the same addresses as the standards and the map, the common holding first steps, each step saying who it is for. Each person's path is their own mirror of it, in their garden. The Leadership Team changes the steps block, never the code. Why: the app used to open over a person's first nine days by counting kept days, which went on 11 November under 'nothing is counted'; opening by what a person has done keeps that rule and lets the app grow again.
9.4: WHAT I BRING, FIRST — offered first on Today, never required (4.2). These are the first questions, before any day is kept: the leaders become the first gift map, and answering is their first chance to say whether the questions are right.
9.5: MY GARDEN — each member's private place: their hope as a gold seed, their gifts, their days, and the steps they've taken drawn as flowers in the standards' four colours. Bare ground is room to grow; no numbers, no scores. Why the name: a garden is somewhere I tend, which says what I do there.
9.6: OUR WOOD — the standards drawn as four groves, a tree for each standard, growing as the community shows it in what it does; the same steps feed it only as community evidence, with no names. It replaces the standards garden built on 13 and 14 November, so each word keeps one meaning. Why a wood: Alan Rayner is a mycologist, and under a wood the trees are joined by threads, each its own centre and all held together, which is Natural Inclusion; a wood also grows at the pace a LERO grows.
9.7: THE GIFT MAP, as peer leaders see it (1.11): the helper notices who might meet whom, a peer leader decides and makes the introduction in person, and the cards of things to do stand beside it.
9.8: SEE IT AS — for builders only, Matthew and David: shows the app as someone outside, someone who has asked to join, a member from day one, a member, a welcomer, a leader or a supporter. It writes nothing as them and never opens anyone's days or notes, and builders stay out of members' lists as trial names already do. Built first, so every screen can be checked as each kind of person sees it. The leaders are told openly, as they were about supporters, and the builders' word 'janitor' never appears on screen.
9.9: WHO BUILDS — weft is the one builder of the app for phase three; Matthew's own Claude Code pauses on the app except for fixes they agree. Labels are drafted as the person's own question, in I and we, run through the language engine, and chosen by the Leadership Team. Why: two builders on one screen wrote over each other's words, and on 14 November the bar went in at noon and came out at four.
9._: THE USER EXPERIENCE — decided 14 November by Matthew, from weft's proposal after weft and David's call, and from Claude's reading of the original proposal and all three phases. The app grows with what a person does, so nothing is counted and it still opens up as people take part. Screens drawn on 14 November in Community Recovery's own look, from the app as it stands. The people on the gift map are samples; the grove sizes in our wood are illustrative.

1.2: WHY A PLACE — today the app is a menu of pages, and each time something matters a link is added to the home screen. A place gives every page a home and lets people move through it knowing where they stand. Rings, positions and 'we are here' are how people already find their way in a community, and the screens can work the same way.

3._: THE BEACH'S OWN STANDARD — places are kept the way the beach already keeps them (pscale:world-genome; block-conventions 4.7): spatial:<world> for the places, nested so each address says what holds it; identity:<world> for how each group holds each place; keeper:<world> for what the place is for. Community Recovery's beach is what that standard calls a compact world, one lived-in place where what happens builds up as its life. The lighthouse stays the sign at the front and points into the landscape.
3.2: A MAP THE APP DRAWS — the landscape kept as the app's own plan: the app draws the common, the four neighbourhoods, the gate and the gardens from what Community Recovery's beach already holds, the lighthouse, which keeps the same homes in the same four parts, and where-and-when, with Matthew's draft (community-recovery-design:Phenomemental 1.295 to 1.297) as the plan it follows. Nothing on the beach is read as a world, every member's passport stays as it is, and the app gets clearer now, which is the aim (community-recovery-design:Phenomemental 1.298). The same addresses can be written to the beach's standard whenever that is chosen.
3.3: A WORLD ON THE LIVE BEACH — spatial:community-recovery, identity:community-recovery and keeper:community-recovery on Community Recovery's own beach, as 1.11113 says: any AI holding bsp-mcp then reads it as a place, CLERO reads the same addresses across LEROs (1.111), and the earth graft works by the standard (1.1113). Three things are settled first. A person's place in a world is their passport's 3, and moving rewrites it (pscale:world-genome 1.2); in the app, 3 was 'What I could use' until 13 November, and what members wrote there stays. identity says how each group holds each place and locks nothing; the colours and keys keep doing that. keeper is the standard's held register, kept from what a person entering is handed (pscale:world-genome 4.1 and 5), while what 1.297 says is meant for every member.
3.4: A WORLD TRIED APART FIRST — the same three blocks on a beach of their own with made-up members, walked by David, Matthew and weft as a member would walk it, before anything is added to Community Recovery's beach; then MAP or WORLD, with what the walk showed.
3.8: DECIDE — how should the landscape be kept: as a map the app draws, as a world on Community Recovery's live beach, or tried as a world apart first? Asked of David, weft and Matthew. MAP, WORLD, APART or NOT YET. Matthew's answer, 14 November: MAP, with the reasons at 4.7.

1.4: THE DRAFT — written on 14 November 2026 at community-recovery-design:Phenomemental 1.295 (the places), 1.296 (who holds each place) and 1.297 (what the place is for), with 1.298 naming what stays open: each place's room for talk, the boards on the common, and the depth of the landscape.
1.5: NATURAL INCLUSION — the shape is Alan Rayner's: each person a distinct centre, a garden of their own, included in a shared neighbourhood, with boundaries as places of relation. What is theirs stays theirs; what happens together is ours (leros-on-the-commons 4).
1.8: DECIDE — is this the foundation every LERO's app stands on: one landscape, laid out to the beach's standard for places, with every screen a view of it? Asked of David, weft and Matthew. Matthew's answer, 14 November: yes for Community Recovery now, kept as a map the app draws that follows the standard's addresses (4.7); for other LEROs once phase one's kit, agreement and ground are in place (1.111).
1._: THE PLACE — one landscape, laid out once, that every screen is a view of. At the centre is the common, where everyone sits down together. Around it are four neighbourhoods, standing where the four sections of the national LERO standards stand: culture and values, support offer, volunteers, and running the place. The gate is on the open edge, where visitors come in and members arrive, and the gardens are each member's own place, private. Inside them sit each LERO's real places: for Community Recovery, Salem Hall and the Allotments. Every home a LERO keeps (its constitution, noticeboard, policies, standards) has one place here, and each new thing gets its place before it is built.

spine.3: WHERE IT CAME FROM — Matthew, on 14 November 2026, the morning after Community Recovery's Leadership Team came into its app: links were gathering on the home screen because people needed to see things, which showed a design problem. spine.9: PROVENANCE — written on 14 November 2026, in the morning, by Claude working with Matthew Bushell (Phenomemental), on the proposal form (function:proposal) beside phase two, from what stood on the beach that day: function:proposal, function:document, pscale:world-genome, block-conventions 4.7, spatial:earth, the lighthouse and where-and-when on beach.communityrecovery.life, spine:leros-on-the-commons and spine:leros-phase-two. spine._: LEROs ON THE COMMONS, PHASE THREE — the place: one landscape that every LERO's app stands on, so people find their way around their community, see where its life is and what each person brings, and the app can grow without becoming a maze. Community Recovery first.

4.1: WHO HOLDS THE PLACE — the house key moves from weft to two caretakers the Leadership Team names, with Matthew holding it beside them as a supporter while they grow into it. The leaders agree to that, every use of the key is recorded where they can see it, and the caretakers say when Matthew's hold ends. Weft hands it over and keeps building through work the caretakers hand on. Supporters are a group of their own: people from partner organisations who help without a vote, Matthew and Willie now. 'Keeper' is not used for Community Recovery's people. Why: the place belongs to the people who answer to members (Matthew's card of 13 November); a skilled holder is needed until the caretakers are confident; and Matthew's hold must be visible and bounded, because he works for The Forward Trust and the constitution keeps partners' employees off the Leadership Team.
4.2: WHAT IS MINE — What I bring holds hope, something I know about, something I can do or make, something I care about, groups I'm part of, and what helps me take part. Each part has its own choice of who sees it: just me, the person who welcomed me, or all members. It is offered first, never required. What someone could use stays in the welcome conversation on paper, and health, treatment and legal matters are never written. Why: asset-based community development starts from people's gifts and dreams, and in recovery hope is often the first thing someone has, sometimes before they believe they have gifts. Recovery capital, when it comes, lives in My garden, framed by the ten-domain Assessment of Recovery Capital with the BARC-10 at intervals, the frame Matthew chose on 26 October; the bridge to the organisation's picture comes later, with a yes for each share, no names, and nothing shown until enough have taken part. Why: it is the frame the field and commissioners recognise; CHIME stays as how Community Recovery already talks about recovery.
4.3: PRIVACY AND AI — Matthew's position of 13 November stands: members' kept days, readable by nobody but the member, are enough privacy on Community Recovery's own beach. The hosting companies' terms on health data are a known risk, written here; phase two is corrected to match. The original proposal's 'helper in your pocket' lives on in Speak: anyone can talk rather than type. Inside the app the only AI helps the peer leaders see who might meet whom; the peer leaders make the introductions, and the AI never contacts members. A member may connect their own AI, such as Claude or ChatGPT, through a connector, or in future with their own API key (not encouraged); it reads only that member's own garden and shares, and the rest of the members' circle stays inside the app. Why: the peer is the spine of support, and other members' words should not pass to someone else's AI company. The privacy notice says all of this.
4.4: TALKING SAFELY — each place's room for talk opens once two things are true: the Leadership Team has adopted Community Recovery's safeguarding policy, first in the policy run-through, and rooms can be read by members only. Today's rooms carry on: the noticeboard with its replies, each person's own room, and the policies' room. Private talk between two members stays paused, as decided on 13 November; any private channel is a separate decision under the safeguarding policy. Every room, when it opens, has someone named to look after it and a clear way to raise a concern, and the membership form's promise holds in the app: volunteers may get advice or share what is needed, and will tell people where they can. Why: each room is another open thread to look after, and until the members' circle exists anything said in one can be read beyond the membership.
4.5: JOINING — part one of the membership form has two digital doors: Ask to join, for anyone, and an invitation from a member. Part two is always in person, on paper, with a welcoming volunteer, and nothing digital is attached to it. Part one in the app makes someone a participant; part two makes them a member with a vote. The welcomers' list, held by Liz and Jo-Jo, is the bridge between the two. Why: the welcome is a human relationship carried on face to face, and the constitution gives the vote to a signed membership form.
4.6: MONEY AND REACH — the work costs weft's building and David's time, and phase three says so. The original proposal's three conditions stand: Community Recovery earns, the beach is sustained, and volunteers and members pay nothing. James's offer of a small grant (13 November: Community Recovery the applicant, David the supplier) is the route once the basic standard exists, when there is something real to show a funder. Role-play and James's community studio are a future strand the landscape is ready for, offered to the community when they want it, the Leadership Team deciding. Other LEROs: 1.111. Why: 'costs nothing' hid David's and weft's time, and phase three asks more of them than the earlier phases.
4.7: HOW THE LANDSCAPE IS KEPT (the card at 1.38) — Matthew's answer: a map the app draws, now. A world on Community Recovery's beach waits until what a member's passport 3 holds is settled after What I bring, and until what identity and keeper would mean for Community Recovery is settled; any moving through the place is tried apart first. Why: the app gets clearer now, which is the aim, and nothing new is added to a beach real people are using before it must be.

4.9: MY DAYS AND WHERE THEY REST — brought back, at the scale of a corner, never the centre. Keeping a day offers Sundial's six ways a day is told, and the person taps where it rests, or just keeps it (1.191); holding the heart and letting go opens where my days rest (1.192); six small circles at the edge of My garden show it, in one plain sentence naming only what is there, with no numbers (1.195); the heart casts the real sun's shadow, set by the town, the phone's own location optional, worked out on the phone and never sent. It needs no AI: the person chooses. Where it came from: phase one, 26 October 2026, 'the way in is P6, as in Sundial' (leros-on-the-commons 1.17241), with its named gap, the bridge from Sundial to recovery capital (1.111); phase two kept 'holding the heart' for after privacy is settled (leros-phase-two 1.11111). Why: P6 is a way of reflecting on your reflections; a resting place a person chooses is a shape, which keeps 'nothing is counted'; and it is the person's own end of the bridge to recovery capital, which an AI can read later (5.2, 5.4). 5._: HELD IN VIEW — Matthew's Sundial (founded 21 October 2026 as a web page; since 3 November one app on the phone, formerly the pocket beach and Rockpool; release 0.10.4 of 10 November, downloadable from his repository) carries more than phase three builds. It is laid out here strand by strand so David and weft can scrutinise each one, separate any, and take up what fits, and so nothing Matthew has made limits anything else. Each strand says what stands, what comes next and who carries it. Only 5.1 is in phase three's build; the rest are the developmental path beyond it.
5.1: MY DAYS AND WHERE THEY REST, WITH NO AI — in phase three's build, as 4.9 decides. NOW: written into the screens' lines (1.191, 1.192, 1.195), with a drawing on the page. NEXT: weft builds it after See it as and the steps, on the private copy first (1.1111). Carried by weft, steered by Matthew.
5.2: AN AI INSIDE THE APP, ON A SHARED KEY — a design option, kept open. Phase one already describes it (leros-on-the-commons 1.17241, 'with the API, the commissioner's key'): it reads a member's tellings into the ten recovery capital domains, asks a question from another of the six ways a day is told (Sundial's acuity), and suggests what might strengthen a quiet domain; and more, as the design grows. Conditions before any real member uses it: who pays is named (phase one says the commissioner); the host's terms allow health data; the member says yes, each time; the data controller is named; and it follows the LERO's own recipes (5.5). CLAUDE'S WEIGHED CONCERN, kept here: this sends members' words about their days to an AI company, the same risk 4.3 names for hosting, and only 5.4 avoids it; so 5.2 should not come before its conditions are met. NEXT: David and weft scrutinise the design (5.8).
5.3: THREE AIs, NAMED APART — so nobody confuses them. The LERO helper, David's (built in mid-October 2026, happyseaurchin.com/ask/lero-helper): public, answering anyone about LEROs from trusted places only, and alerting a person when someone needs one; it grew from Matthew's answer to weft of 3 October. Our helper: notices who might meet whom for the peer leaders and never contacts a member (4.3; leros-on-the-commons 1.1728). A member's companion: theirs alone, for their own days (5.2 or 5.4). On 15 October Matthew chose a Community Recovery agent of its own for the meeting room over the LERO helper; who pays for the LERO helper's use was still open with David.
5.4: SUNDIAL ON THE PHONE — a local AI (Gemma, downloaded to the phone), a local copy of the beach and the person's own shell, so a member's days never leave their phone. It carries the real sun's shadow, set from a town or the phone's rough location and never sent; the spiral of days; P6, with the companion marking where each moment rests and the person correcting (Matthew, 4 November); and the online beach as a switch, sending only the person's own words, each time with their yes. Phase two names it as an answer to the health-data hosting problem (leros-phase-two 1.11119). STATE: in development and in use on Matthew's own phone; his next step (3 November) is a second person's hands. Postponed for phase three's build, held here so it is never lost. Carried by Matthew; its state at github.com/Phenomemental/happyseaurchin-beach, pocket-beach/STATUS.md.
5.5: RECIPES — behaviour lives in blocks, so the way an AI greets, hosts and keeps days is written in sentences a person can change, never in code; Matthew proved it on his own phone (3 November: editing his cook's lines changed how Sundial behaves). A LERO could write its own recipes with its members: co-production in the literal sense, and community capital a LERO can show. Recipes stand apart from the local AI: any AI the app carries, local (5.4) or on a shared key (5.2), could follow a LERO's recipe block. An intention, written in the Sundial report of 10 November; offered to nobody yet.
5.6: THE REAL SUN — in the app, the heart's shadow set by Community Recovery's town, so no location is asked (4.9); in Sundial, the sun from where the person stands. Matthew holds the sun as the day's rhythm, away from productivity (3 November): people see their experience in rhythm with their environment, as a solar system.
